newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks rise, unaffected by bank limit delay.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks rise, unaffected by bank limit delay.

text.p: Thai stocks gained slightly for the second day on Thursday in a technical rebound as investors shrugged off the central bank's postponement of measures to limit imported foreign loans for relending in the Thai market.
The SET index closed 12.78 points higher to 929.61 on 3.5 billion baht turnover. The SET-50 index rose 1.18 points to 69.92.
"The postponement of the new measures by the Bank of Thailand will help the money market but it won't help the Thai economy or the stock market," said Thanawat Patchimkul of Seamico Securities.

The Bank of Thailand said on Thursday it had decided to postpone new measures to limit the amount of foreign loans that offshore units of foreign and local banks can import for relending in the domestic market.

"It's good news for the money market and will help keep liquidity high. But there is not much reaction from the stock market because it is viewed more as a matter for financial institutions than as an equities matter," said Thanadech Mahapokai, first assistant vice president at Book Club Finance and Securities Plc.
"The market wasn't active today as investors waited for finance companies to submit their balance sheets for the third quarter on Monday," said Thanawat.
Brokers said they anticipated third quarter results of finance firms would not be good.
Bangkok Bank, Thailand's largest commercial bank, topped the active list, gaining three baht to 188. National Finance and Securities gained 2.50 to 51.50 and Advanced Info Service surged 22 to 338.
